stories.headline: Free festive event at Orchard House in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Families in Wisbech are invited to a Christmas Wonderland event at Orchard House care home later this month. The two-day celebration takes place on Friday, December 18, and Saturday, December 19, running from 2pm until 8pm each day. 

Visitors can enjoy a craft zone, browse various gift stalls, and meet Father Christmas. While entry and visits with Father Christmas are free, bookings for the meeting are required. Children under 11 will receive a gift. Refreshments and items from the stalls will be available to purchase separately. The event is open to all local residents, providing an opportunity to meet the care home team while enjoying the festive activities.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital moves orthotics service to South Lynn
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has relocated its orthotics service to the health hub on Cambridge Road, off Nar Ouse Way. The team, which provides assessments and fittings for braces and splints, began operating from the new site on Monday, November 23. All adult appointments are now held at this purpose-built facility.

Hospital officials state that clinics at the North Cambridgeshire Hospital in Wisbech and the Roxburgh Unit are not affected by this change. Patients can continue to use the existing contact number, 01553 214652, for enquiries. The move follows the relocation of the hospital’s dermatology and midwifery services to the same South Lynn location.

stories.headline: New vision test proposals for drivers over 70
stories.brief: Motorists aged 70 and older could be required to undergo mandatory eye examinations every three years. Under new proposals reported by the BBC, these regular checks would be introduced to ensure drivers continue to meet the necessary vision standards for road safety. No further details regarding the implementation of these plans have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: New social events announced at local pub
stories.brief: A pub is launching two new regular events for the community. The venue has introduced a dedicated singles’ night alongside a brand-new quiz evening. These additions aim to provide fresh social opportunities for local residents. Further details regarding the specific dates and times for these events are expected to be available through the establishment directly.

stories.headline: A47 closed following HGV collision near Wisbech
stories.brief:
A lorry driver has escaped with minor injuries after their vehicle jackknifed and hit a tree on the A47. The incident happened between Wisbech and Guyhirn at 12:50 am yesterday. 

Emergency services attended the scene to manage the initial response and close the road. The route remained shut for most of the day while crews carried out a complex recovery operation for the fully loaded HGV. Motorists are advised that the road has since reopened.

stories.headline: New Lidl plans submitted for King’s Lynn site
stories.brief:
Lidl has resubmitted plans for a new supermarket and two drive-thru units at Morston Point, near the Hardwick Retail Park in King’s Lynn. The proposal comes just weeks after West Norfolk Council rejected a previous application due to concerns regarding highway safety and access. 

The updated plans include a new junction and an extension to the nearby roundabout to improve traffic flow. The supermarket would feature 117 car parking spaces and 16 bicycle bays. If approved, the store is expected to create 40 jobs, with a further 20 to 30 roles potentially added by the drive-thru units. Lidl states these changes are designed to address the specific reasons for the council's earlier refusal.

stories.headline: Tudor history revealed at March church
stories.brief: New details have emerged regarding the historic ceiling at a church in March. Reports indicate that the structure features angelic designs dating back to the Tudor period. Further information on the origins of the ceiling has been highlighted by the BBC.

stories.headline: Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police have launched a murder investigation following the discovery of a woman’s body at a property on Alexandra Road in Wisbech. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 9:50pm on Saturday. The victim has been named as Vera. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the property on suspicion of murder and remains in custody. 

A post-mortem examination is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon. Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee has described the death as an isolated incident. Authorities are asking anyone with information to contact them online or by calling 101, quoting Operation Emeth.

stories.headline: Looking back at local news from November 1996
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at the headlines from late November 1996. In Hockwold, darts players completed a 12-hour charity marathon, raising funds for the cancer ward at Addenbrooke’s Hospital. Meanwhile, in West Lynn, the Reverend Andrew Davey voiced criticism over a local initiative to fund two part-time special constables. The scheme, intended to tackle vandalism, relied on community contributions and business donations, leading the rector to question why residents should pay twice for policing services. 

Elsewhere in the region, West Norfolk councillors approved an £835,000 plan for a new Red Cross centre in Downham, while receivers were appointed at the Saddlebow Road speedway stadium in King's Lynn.

stories.headline: Pedestrian seriously injured in two-car collision
stories.brief: A pedestrian has been left with serious injuries following a road traffic collision involving two cars. Emergency services were called to the scene to attend to the casualty. No further details regarding the exact location or the condition of those involved have been released at this time. Motorists are advised to remain alert when travelling through the area.

stories.headline: Conservative candidate selected for Ely and East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A district councillor has been chosen as the Conservative Party candidate for the Ely and East Cambridgeshire constituency. The selection was reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News.

stories.headline: Fenland Christmas gift appeal returns for ninth year
stories.brief:
The Fenland Neighbourhood Policing Team has launched its annual Christmas gift appeal to support local children in need. Now in its ninth year, the campaign is seeking donations of new items including toys, books, puzzles, sports equipment, and beauty sets for children aged from birth to over 11. 

Donations can be dropped off at the Tesco store in March or at Awdry House on Ramnoth Road in Wisbech until December 16. Please ensure gifts are new and placed in a sealed bag, but left unwrapped. Online deliveries can also be sent to Sally Fairbrass at Awdry House. All contributions will be distributed to local families by social workers after the appeal closes.

stories.headline: Looking back at West Norfolk community fundraising efforts
stories.brief:
The Lynn News has revisited a series of charitable initiatives from November 2013 and 2014. Across West Norfolk, residents and organisations supported a variety of causes, including food banks, the Royal British Legion’s Poppy Appeal, and the West Norfolk Riding for the Disabled. 

Students from the College of West Anglia raised funds for the Benjamin Foundation, while other projects saw improvements to local school facilities and donations to medical charities. From caravan park events in Snettisham to black-tie balls in King’s Lynn, these past efforts highlight the community spirit shown by local groups, schools, and businesses during those two years.

stories.headline: Local editors warn government over online news plans
stories.brief:
Editors from across the UK, including the editor of the Fenland Citizen, have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. The group argues that the suggested prominence regime is unworkable and could threaten the future of local journalism by distorting the news marketplace. 

The letter highlights fears that the policy could lead to fewer local news sources for communities. Instead, the editors are calling for alternative support, such as ensuring fair payment from digital platforms and increasing government advertising spend in local titles. The signatories believe these changes are necessary to protect the sustainability of the local news ecosystem.

stories.headline: Teenager sentenced following high-speed police pursuit on A47
stories.brief:
An 18-year-old man has been handed a suspended prison sentence after a dangerous police pursuit across Norfolk. Ellis Rabey-Prosser, of Mildenhall, reached speeds of 100mph and drove the wrong way around a roundabout in Swaffham during the incident on October 6. The pursuit concluded when he crashed into a lamppost at the Hardwick roundabout in King’s Lynn.

Rabey-Prosser pleaded guilty to multiple charges, including dangerous driving and driving while disqualified. At Norwich Magistrates’ Court, he received a 12-month prison sentence, suspended for two years. He has also been disqualified from driving for a further two years and must pay £227 in costs. Police confirmed the driver had altered his vehicle's number plate before the pursuit began.

stories.headline: House of Commons report highlights regional eye screening gaps
stories.brief: A new report from the House of Commons Library has identified regional disparities in eye screening services for children. The findings suggest that access to these health checks varies significantly depending on where families live. While the data highlights these differences across the country, it does not specify how individual areas within the Fens are affected. The full report is now available for public review through the House of Commons Library website.

stories.headline: RAF memorial sign vandalised in Spalding
stories.brief: A memorial sign dedicated to the RAF in Spalding has been targeted by vandals. The site was defaced with Nazi swastikas. Local authorities are currently dealing with the incident.

stories.headline: Liberal Democrats gain control of county council
stories.brief: The Liberal Democrats have secured control of the county council. The party reached this position following recent political developments. No further details regarding the specific council or the margin of the result have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech roads closed following burst water main
stories.brief:
Drivers in Wisbech are being advised to find alternative routes this afternoon following the closure of South Brink and Alexandra Road. Police were called to the area at 1:45pm today after reports of a burst water main causing flooding. 

Emergency services, including the fire service, are currently at the scene dealing with the incident. Both roads have been closed with immediate effect to allow crews to work safely. Motorists are encouraged to plan their journeys accordingly and avoid the immediate vicinity while the situation is resolved.

stories.headline: Local editors warn government over online news plans
stories.brief:
Editors from across the UK have written to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy to express concerns over proposed government plans for online news. The group, which includes editors from local titles across the country, warns that the current proposals are unworkable and could threaten the future of local journalism.

The letter argues that the suggested prominence regime could distort the local news market and reduce the number of news sources available to communities. Instead, the editors are calling for alternative support, such as ensuring fair payment from digital platforms and increasing the share of government advertising directed toward local news outlets. The signatories believe these changes are necessary to protect a sustainable and plural local news ecosystem.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council and King’s Lynn Town FC join forces for White Ribbon Day
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council and King’s Lynn Town Football Club have launched a joint campaign to tackle male violence, harassment, and abuse against women and girls. Marking White Ribbon Day, the partnership has released a video featuring players and staff encouraging the community to challenge sexist behaviour and inappropriate comments. 

The initiative is part of a three-year action plan to promote a culture of respect. Officials are urging the public to speak up against abuse and are highlighting support services for victims of domestic violence. Those seeking help can contact the Leeway charity on 0300 561 0077 or the National Domestic Abuse Helpline on 0808 2000 247. Further information is available on the council and football club’s social media channels.

stories.headline: NHS trust adopts LEGO therapy for neurodivergent children
stories.brief: A Cambridgeshire NHS trust has officially adopted a LEGO-based therapy programme designed to support neurodivergent children. The initiative uses the popular building blocks as a tool to assist with development and social interaction. The programme is now being implemented across the trust to provide additional support for young people with neurodivergent conditions.

stories.headline: B1099 near March to face further closure
stories.brief: The B1099 road near March is set to close once again. This follows the recent completion of a one point five million pound trial on the route, which had only reopened to traffic a few weeks ago. Motorists who use the road are advised to plan their journeys accordingly as further disruption is expected.

stories.headline: New film about the making of Rocky showing in Wisbech
stories.brief:
The film I Play Rocky is now showing at The Light cinema in Wisbech. The 12A-rated production stars Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone, documenting his struggle to write and star in the original 1976 boxing classic. The movie also features AnnaSophia Robb, PJ Byrne, and Toby Kebbell. 

The film explores the challenges Stallone faced while trying to get his script produced on a limited budget. Despite the title, the production focuses more on the behind-the-scenes story than the boxing matches themselves. Local cinema-goers can catch the film at The Light now.

stories.headline: College of West Anglia students showcase films at Lynn Film Festival
stories.brief:
Students from the College of West Anglia have showcased their creative work at the sixth annual Lynn Film Festival. Level 3 Creative Media learners produced a variety of short films, gaining experience in screenwriting, directing, and editing. Beyond their filmmaking, the students helped organise the festival’s preview evening at the Corn Exchange, with hospitality students providing catering for the event. 

The films will be screened to the public on Thursday, November 26, and Sunday, November 29. Those interested in attending can purchase tickets through the King’s Lynn Corn Exchange box office or via their website. Organisers have praised the students for their professional contribution to this year’s festival programme.

stories.headline: Murder investigation underway in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police have launched a murder investigation following the death of a 61-year-old woman in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Alexandra Road at 9:50pm on Saturday. A 62-year-old man, who was arrested at the scene on suspicion of murder, is currently in hospital. He is expected to remain there for a few days before being returned to police custody.

Detectives say they are not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident, which they believe to be isolated. A post-mortem examination is scheduled for Thursday. Anyone with information is asked to contact police on 101, quoting Operation Emeth.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn literary lunch raises funds for local charities
stories.brief:
A literary lunch held in King’s Lynn has raised nearly £500 for charity. Soroptimist International King’s Lynn hosted the event on Sunday, November 15, featuring guest speaker and biographer Midge Gillies. Attendees heard about the lives of pioneering female pilots, the subject of Ms Gillies' latest book, 'Atlantic Furies'.

The funds collected during the afternoon will be donated to the charities Break and GirlGuiding Lynn. Organisers hope the stories of these historic aviators will inspire young women to pursue their own ambitions.

stories.headline: Conservative candidate selected for Ely
stories.brief: The Conservative Party has announced its candidate for the upcoming election in Ely. The individual selected for the role is a councillor who previously made history by becoming the youngest person elected to the position at the age of 18. No further details regarding the candidate's identity or the specific election date have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Man sentenced for prison-based burglary plot
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced for orchestrating a burglary while serving time in a prison cell. Lincolnshire Police confirmed the conviction, which also included charges related to traffic offences. The individual was sentenced for his role in coordinating the burglary from custody, alongside the separate driving-related matters. No further details regarding the length of the sentence or the location of the offences have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Fenland teenager sentenced to Young Offender Institution
stories.brief: A teenager from the Fenland area has been sent to a Young Offender Institution. The sentencing follows a breach of a court order. No further details regarding the individual or the nature of the original offence have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal following deliberate car fire in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Firefighters were called to Onyx Court in Wisbech on Saturday night to deal with a vehicle blaze. A crew from Thorney arrived at the scene at 10:01pm and used a hose reel to extinguish the fire. The incident is being treated as deliberate, and the crew had returned to their station by 10:45pm.

Police are now asking anyone with information regarding the fire to come forward. You can submit a report through the police website or contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555111.

stories.headline: National operator First Bus acquires King’s Lynn company Lynx
stories.brief:
The King’s Lynn-based bus operator Lynx has been acquired by the national firm First Bus. The move aims to expand the company's network across North and West Norfolk. Lynx, which was founded in 2014, currently manages 25 routes with a fleet of 38 vehicles and 80 staff members.

The existing management team will remain in place, and Lynx will continue to operate as a separate unit within the First Bus portfolio. Founders Julian Patterson, Andy Warnes, and Steve Challis stated that the partnership will help protect the business while providing access to national investment and expertise. First Bus says it intends to build on the existing reputation of the service to encourage further bus travel in the region.

stories.headline: Children in King’s Lynn receive surprise books and bears
stories.brief:
Youngsters attending a Munchkin and Me session in King’s Lynn have received a surprise gift of teddy bears and reading packs. The items were donated by the Build-A-Bear Foundation and the charity BookTrust as part of a national gifting initiative. 

Each child was given a bear to act as a reading companion, alongside a pack containing books and activities. The donation is part of the Bookstart programme, which aims to support families in sharing stories together. Organisers hope the gifts will encourage children to develop a love of reading and help parents incorporate storytelling into their daily routines. Around 1,000 bears have been distributed to children across the UK through this partnership.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn marks start of festive season
stories.brief:
More than 1,500 people gathered in King’s Lynn’s Tuesday Market Place on Sunday for the town’s annual Christmas lights switch-on. The event featured an afternoon of live entertainment, including performances from the St Martha’s School Choir, the band Above All Else, and singer Sarah Mai. 

West Norfolk Mayor, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, officially illuminated the town’s festive displays at 5pm. Organised by West Norfolk Council, the celebration was hosted by Jeremy Durrant. Local officials have thanked the performers and the public for attending the event, which marked the official start of the countdown to Christmas in the town.

stories.headline: New coffee shop to open in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new branch of Esquires The Organic Coffee Co. is scheduled to open in King’s Lynn this Wednesday, November 25. The café is located on the High Street at the site of the former Burtons and Coneys menswear store. 

Signage has been visible at the premises for several weeks, and preparations are now nearing completion with furniture and lighting installed. The franchise, which already operates a site in Swaffham, specialises in organic and Fairtrade coffee. This opening follows the brand’s announcement in October that it would be expanding into the town.

stories.headline: Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police remain at a property on Alexandra Road in Wisbech following the death of a 61-year-old woman. Officers were called to the scene at approximately 9:50pm on Saturday. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the location on suspicion of murder and is currently in police custody.

Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee of the major crime unit has described the event as an isolated incident and confirmed that officers are not searching for anyone else. Residents with information are encouraged to contact the police online or by calling 101, quoting Operation Emeth. Investigations at the site are ongoing.

stories.headline: West Norfolk students showcase musical talents at Marshland High School
stories.brief:
Marshland High School in West Walton has hosted an annual musical workshop for students across the West Norfolk Academies Trust. Fifty-two pupils, including 41 from primary schools and 11 from the host secondary school, spent the day developing their skills on brass, woodwind, string, and piano instruments.

The event saw a 20 per cent increase in participation compared to last year. Students worked in wind and string ensembles before performing for families in the school hall. Organisers say the initiative aims to build confidence and teamwork, providing young musicians with opportunities to apply skills learned during their weekly lessons. The workshop is part of a wider programme that rotates annually between the trust’s various high schools.

stories.headline: Solihull Moors FC confirms partnership renewal
stories.brief: Solihull Moors Football Club has announced that Midland Eye will continue as an official club partner. The agreement sees the renewal of the existing commercial relationship between the two organisations.

stories.headline: Construction begins on new £24 million Wisbech school
stories.brief:
Work has officially started on a new £24 million secondary school in Wisbech. Being built by Henry Brothers on the grounds of the Thomas Clarkson Academy, the facility will provide 600 places for students in years seven to eleven. The school will be managed by the Brooke Weston Trust and is designed to address the rising demand for secondary education in the area.

The development features sustainable design elements, including a bio-solar roof and photovoltaic panels to improve energy efficiency. The project was procured through the Department for Education construction framework and is expected to provide a modern learning environment for the growing local community.

stories.headline: West Norfolk schools support Children in Need
stories.brief:
Pupils and staff across the West Norfolk Academies Trust took part in fundraising activities for BBC Children in Need on Friday, November 13. Schools in Hunstanton, King’s Lynn, Clenchwarton, Heacham, and Walpole Cross Keys joined the national appeal by swapping uniforms for yellow, spots, and Pudsey Bear ears.

Participants engaged in various classroom activities, games, and assemblies to learn about the charity’s work supporting disadvantaged children. Schools involved included Smithdon High, Heacham Infant and Nursery, West Lynn Primary, Clenchwarton Primary, and Walpole Cross Keys Primary. Families were encouraged to contribute to the cause through digital donations, with staff highlighting the importance of teaching students about responsibility and supporting those in difficult situations.

stories.headline: Conservative majority secured in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: The Conservative Party has gained a majority on East Cambridgeshire District Council. This shift in control follows the defection of a former Liberal Democrat councillor to the Conservative group. The change in political balance was confirmed following the announcement of the councillor's move.

stories.headline: Busy month of community projects for Priory Rotary Club
stories.brief:
The Priory Rotary Club has completed a series of community projects across the King’s Lynn area. Volunteers recently planted a new oak tree and created a wildflower bed at Wootton Park. The club also hosted its annual technology tournament for students from five local schools, and served a harvest lunch to 80 elderly residents in Dersingham. 

Financial support has also been provided to several charities, including the Tapping House hospice and the Fairstead Community Shop. Looking ahead, the club is preparing for its annual Swimarathon, scheduled for February 6 at St James Pool in King’s Lynn. Those interested in joining the club or learning more about their upcoming events can visit the Priory Rotary website.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital specialist wins national mentoring award
stories.brief:
A health play specialist at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been honoured with a national award. Nicola Wright received the Starlight Mentor of the Year Award 2026 at a ceremony in London on November 10. The accolade recognises her work in training the next generation of specialists who use therapeutic play to support children through medical treatment.

Ms Wright was nominated by her apprentice, Claire Burrell, who credited her mentor with building the confidence needed to succeed in the role. The hospital’s play team works across the Rudham ward, helping young patients manage fears surrounding procedures and long-term hospital stays. Chief nurse Dawn Collins praised Ms Wright for her dedication to both patient care and staff development.

stories.headline: Mixed FA Cup results for Peterborough United Women
stories.brief: Peterborough United Women have successfully progressed to the next round of the FA Cup. However, it was a difficult day for the club’s under-21 side, who suffered a heavy defeat in their respective fixture. The results were reported by the Peterborough Telegraph.

stories.headline: Looking back at local news from the archives
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at stories from the Lynn News archives during the month of November. In 2014, children’s author Paeony Lewis visited Swaffham Infants School to celebrate the opening of a new £10,000 library. That same year, Smithdon High School student Evan Andrews took the top prize in the Hunstanton and District Festival of Arts photography competition.

In 2017, Denver-based singer Mike Pye raised over £640 for the Children in Need appeal through performances in Downham. Also in 2017, a collection of jewellery belonging to the late ballroom dancing legend Peggy Spencer was sold at a Christmas fair in Gaywood to support local causes.

stories.headline: Plymouth Argyle manager looks to regroup following Peterborough loss
stories.brief: Plymouth Argyle manager Tom Cleverley is focusing on his team's recovery following their recent defeat against Peterborough. The boss is aiming to rally his squad after what has been described as a poor performance in the match.

stories.headline: Eleven road closures scheduled across Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised to plan their journeys carefully over the coming days. A total of eleven road closures are currently in place throughout the county this week. Drivers are encouraged to check local travel updates before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these disruptions.

stories.headline: Murder investigation launched in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Police have opened a murder investigation following the death of a 61-year-old woman in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Alexandra Road at approximately 9:50pm yesterday evening, where the woman was found deceased. A 62-year-old man was arrested at the location on suspicion of murder and remains in custody.

Detective Inspector Andrew Moralee of the Major Crime Unit has described the event as an isolated incident and confirmed that police are not seeking any other suspects. Specialist officers remain at the scene to continue their enquiries. Anyone with information regarding the case is asked to contact the police via 101 or their website, quoting Operation Emeth.

stories.headline: Remembering a long-serving King’s Lynn factory worker
stories.brief: We take a look back at a long-standing career at the Campbell’s soup factory in King’s Lynn. In November 1996, Ken Durrant of Gaywood retired after 37 years of service. Mr Durrant was one of the first employees at the Hardwick Road site and spent 22 of those years working in the security hut. He was one of only two staff members to reach such a milestone at the company. Mr Durrant was joined by his wife and family for a farewell presentation with his colleagues to mark the end of his lengthy career.

stories.headline: Plans for Cambridgeshire council merger to be revealed
stories.brief: Plans regarding a potential merger of councils in Cambridgeshire are expected to be announced soon. Details of the proposals have not yet been released, but the upcoming announcement is set to outline the future structure of local government in the area. Residents across the Fens are advised to watch for further updates as more information becomes available regarding how these changes might affect local services and administration.

stories.headline: Safety improvements planned for West Lynn junction
stories.brief:
Safety work is set to begin next month at the junction of Clenchwarton Road and the East Coast Business Park in West Lynn. Norfolk County Council is investing £16,500 to address a history of collisions at the site, with a specific focus on protecting cyclists.

Starting December 7, the two-week project will include new kerb build-outs, extended cycle paths, and updated signage. Temporary four-way traffic signals will be in operation throughout the works, which are subject to weather conditions. Local businesses requiring specific access arrangements are being asked to contact the highways department in advance. Further details regarding the project can be found on the Norfolk County Council website.

stories.headline: Funding bid submitted for Peterborough’s New Theatre
stories.brief: A bid for funding has been launched to modernise the New Theatre building in Peterborough. The proposal aims to secure investment to upgrade the city venue. No further details regarding the scale of the project or the specific improvements planned have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Free home energy support available across the East of England
stories.brief: Residents across the East of England are being offered free support regarding home energy. The initiative is being provided by the organisation Groundwork East. The service aims to assist households throughout the region with energy-related concerns. Further details on how to access this support can be found through the organisation.

stories.headline: Long Sutton headteacher defends school incentive scheme
stories.brief: The headteacher of a school in Long Sutton has spoken out in support of a new incentive programme. The initiative, which has been described as a "duvet day," has been introduced at the school to encourage attendance and engagement among pupils. While the scheme has attracted attention, the school leadership maintains that the policy is a positive step for the student body. No further details regarding the specific criteria for the incentive have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Coronation Fountain to be unveiled in March
stories.brief: A historic landmark is set to be revealed to the public in Cambridgeshire. The Coronation Fountain in the town of March has been prepared for its official unveiling. The project marks a significant addition to the local area, with the fountain now ready for its debut. Residents and visitors are expected to see the completed site shortly.

stories.headline: Fraser Dawbarns to sponsor Customer Care award at 2027 Fenland Business Awards
stories.brief:
Solicitors firm Fraser Dawbarns has been announced as the sponsor for the Customer Care category at the upcoming Fenland Citizen Business Awards. The firm, which operates offices in March and Wisbech, will support the accolade at the ceremony held on Friday, March 19, 2027, at the Wisbech St Mary Sports and Community Centre.

Organisers are now accepting nominations for all eight award categories until 5pm on Wednesday, January 6. Businesses interested in entering are encouraged to visit the Fenland Business Awards website to review the criteria. The event aims to celebrate local innovation and success, with Whitings LLP returning as the headline sponsor for the evening.

stories.headline: Birmingham teenager sentenced following Lynn nightclub incident
stories.brief:
A 19-year-old man from Birmingham has been handed a six-month conditional discharge after admitting to being drunk and disorderly in King’s Lynn. Brayden Tonks was arrested in the early hours of October 17 following a confrontation with door staff and police on Norfolk Street. 

During the incident at 2:45am, Tonks swore at officers and behaved aggressively. Appearing before Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Tonks apologised for his actions and promised the court it would not happen again. In addition to the conditional discharge, he was ordered to pay £40 in court costs and a £26 victim surcharge.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn arts society reaches milestone with food bank donation
stories.brief:
The Arts Society King’s Lynn has reached a significant milestone by donating its 1,000th art and craft pack to the town’s food bank. The project, which began in 2020, provides children from families using the food bank with creative materials and a reading book for Christmas. Each gift is presented in a handmade fabric bag, created with support from Norfolk Creative Arts and the Wootton Crafters.

Funding for this year’s packs was provided by local businesses and charities, including Mars Foods and Hayes and Storr Solicitors. Distribution of the gifts is scheduled to begin at the start of December. Food bank officials have expressed their gratitude for the ongoing support, noting the positive impact these donations have on local families.

stories.headline: Arrest made following police presence in Cambridgeshire village
stories.brief: Police have confirmed an arrest was made after armed officers were deployed to a village in Cambridgeshire. The operation took place following reports of an incident in the area. Authorities have not provided further details regarding the nature of the call-out or the identity of the individual taken into custody. Residents are advised that there is no ongoing threat to the public.

stories.headline: Nominations closing for 2027 West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
stories.brief:
Businesses in West Norfolk have just one week left to submit nominations for the 2027 Mayor’s Business Awards. Organisers are particularly encouraging entries for the Environmental Champion category, which recognises firms demonstrating a strong commitment to sustainability and reducing their environmental impact.

The awards, now in their 38th year, feature 11 different categories. Nominations must be submitted by 5pm on Friday, November 27. The winners will be announced at a ceremony held at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn on Friday, March 5. Last year’s Environmental Champion award was presented to British Sugar’s Wissington site for their work in reducing carbon emissions. Further details on how to enter can be found via the Lynn News.

stories.headline: Peterborough United secure away victory
stories.brief: Peterborough United have claimed a win in their latest League One fixture. The team defeated Plymouth Argyle with a final score of two-nil. The result was confirmed following the match highlights reported by Sky Sports.

stories.headline: Norfolk councillors scrutinise hospital service review
stories.brief:
Norfolk County Council’s Health Overview Scrutiny Committee has examined a new ‘Case for Change’ report from the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group. The review outlines potential service adjustments at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, citing workforce shortages and a projected £53 million deficit by 2034.

Councillors raised concerns that proposed changes could force West Norfolk residents to travel to Norwich for care. During the meeting, Councillor Alexandra Kemp warned that longer travel times on the A47 could negatively impact patient outcomes. While no final decisions have been made, the committee has called for greater transparency and clarity regarding the potential impact on local families and the wider healthcare system.

stories.headline: College of West Anglia students stage Legally Blonde production
stories.brief:
Performing arts students at the College of West Anglia’s King’s Lynn campus have completed a two-day run of a musical inspired by Legally Blonde. The production, which took place on November 17 and 18, featured students from the Level 2 and Level 3 UAL Performing Arts courses. 

Course director Paul Greenwood noted that the students took full responsibility for the project, including casting and directing the show. Participants highlighted the experience as a valuable opportunity to develop their acting, singing, and dance skills. The college stated that the production allowed students to gain practical experience in the industry while building confidence and teamwork ahead of their future careers.

stories.headline: Thousands gather for Peterborough Christmas lights switch-on
stories.brief: Thousands of people have attended the annual Christmas lights switch-on event in Peterborough. The large crowds gathered in the city centre to mark the start of the festive season.

stories.headline: East Anglian village named among the region's best
stories.brief: A village located one hour from Cambridge has been highlighted for its picturesque appearance. Reports describe the area as featuring colourful cottages and hosting what is being called the best pub in East Anglia. The location is being promoted for its aesthetic appeal to those living in the surrounding region.

stories.headline: Students protest toilet policy at University Academy Long Sutton
stories.brief: Pupils at University Academy Long Sutton have staged a protest regarding changes to the school's toilet regulations. The demonstration follows the introduction of new rules concerning student access to facilities at the site. Further details regarding the specific nature of the policy changes or the school's response have not been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire County Council issues battery disposal advice
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire County Council is reminding residents about the correct procedures for disposing of batteries. The local authority has issued guidance to help the public manage battery waste safely across the county. Residents are encouraged to check the council’s official website for specific instructions on how and where to recycle used batteries. Following these guidelines ensures that hazardous materials are handled correctly and helps prevent potential fire risks associated with improper disposal. Further details regarding local collection points and recycling services are available through the Cambridgeshire County Council online portal.

stories.headline: Wisbech prepares for annual Christmas light switch-on
stories.brief:
Wisbech Town Council has announced details for this year’s Christmas light switch-on, taking place in the town on Sunday, November 29. The event runs from 3pm until 6pm, featuring live stage performances, a fun fair, and a snow park. Families can also visit miniature donkeys, while adults will have access to mulled wine. 

Youngsters are invited to the Market Place to meet Santa and post their Christmas wish lists. The official illumination of the town’s festive lights is scheduled for 5.45pm. Residents are encouraged to attend the afternoon of entertainment as the town marks the start of the festive season.

stories.headline: Wisbech teenager disqualified for drink-driving
stories.brief:
A 19-year-old woman from Wisbech has been banned from the roads after being caught drink-driving in King’s Lynn. Juste Kantautaite, of Southwell Road, was stopped by police on Blackfriars Road at 4:20am on October 18. Officers conducted a breath test after finding her stationary vehicle, which revealed she had 61mcg of alcohol in 100ml of breath, exceeding the legal limit of 35mcg. 

At Lynn Magistrates’ Court, the court heard that Kantautaite had been persuaded to drink while celebrating a friend’s birthday. She pleaded guilty to the offence and has been disqualified from driving for 17 months. In addition to the ban, she must pay a £400 fine, a £160 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

stories.headline: Leicestershire bridge named Britain’s most struck
stories.brief: A bridge in Leicestershire has been identified as the most frequently struck structure in the country. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the site has earned the title of Britain’s most bashed bridge. No further details regarding the specific location or the frequency of these incidents were provided in the report.

stories.headline: Met Office weather update for March
stories.brief: The Met Office has released the latest weather information for March in Cambridgeshire. Residents across the Fens are advised to check the official forecast for the most recent updates regarding local conditions.

stories.headline: West Norfolk businesses explore new contract opportunities
stories.brief:
Local firms have been learning about upcoming development projects at the annual Meet the Buyer event held at Lynn Town Hall. Hosted by West Norfolk Council, the free session connected businesses with organisations delivering major infrastructure schemes, including the new Queen Elizabeth Hospital and the West Winch access road.

Representatives from project teams, such as Skanska and Costain, provided details on procurement and future work packages. Attendees also received advice from support groups like the Norfolk Chamber of Commerce and the College of West Anglia. Councillor Simon Ring stated the event aims to help local companies understand how they can get involved in the area's ongoing investment projects.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following fatal jewellery store robbery
stories.brief: Police are investigating a fatal robbery at a jewellery store. Reports indicate that a man has died following the violent incident. No further details regarding the location or the identity of those involved have been released at this stage. Authorities are expected to provide updates as their enquiries continue.

stories.headline: Body recovered from river in Cambridgeshire search
stories.brief: Police have recovered a body from a river during the search for a missing man from Cambridgeshire. The discovery was reported by the Wisbech Standard. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the specific location of the recovery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New planning applications submitted across Fenland
stories.brief:
A range of new planning applications have been submitted to local councils across the Fens. Among the proposals is a project at 13 Alexandra Road in Wisbech, which seeks to convert and extend an existing building to create three houses and six flats. 

Other notable applications include plans for three new homes on land south of 10 Sutton Road in Leverington, and a proposal to add a new inscription to the war memorial on Broad Street. Additionally, Wisbech Fire Station has submitted plans for a new power back-up generator and fuel tank. Residents can view the full list of planning submissions through their local council’s planning portal.

stories.headline: Two charged following Peterborough jewellery store robbery
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Constabulary has confirmed that two people have been charged in connection with a robbery at a jewellery store in Peterborough. Police have released the details following the incident, though no further information regarding the identities of those charged or the specific location of the shop has been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Man sentenced for soliciting indecent images
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced after soliciting indecent photographs of a child. The offender had contacted a person he believed to be a young girl, requesting images of her wearing a school uniform. The case was reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News.

stories.headline: Local geese to feature in new calendar
stories.brief: A group of geese known for their celebrity status are set to be featured in an upcoming calendar. The birds, which have gained local attention, will be the focus of the new publication. Further details regarding the release of the calendar have not yet been announced.

stories.headline: Concerns raised following banger racing event at Adrian Flux Arena
stories.brief:
A family from Bedfordshire has expressed disappointment following a disagreement with staff at the Adrian Flux Arena in Saddlebow. The group, who attended the Halloween spectacular on October 31, reported issues regarding seating arrangements for disabled spectators. The family claimed they were prevented from using their own chairs in a previously permitted area, leading to them being split up.

Arena director Keith Chapman stated that safety rules restricting chairs to the back row are clearly signposted, though he acknowledged the difficulty stewards face in enforcing these policies. The family has called for the venue to clarify its rules, particularly regarding accessibility for those unable to stand for long periods.

stories.headline: Thousands expected for Peterborough Christmas lights switch-on
stories.brief: Thousands of people are expected to gather in Peterborough for the city's annual Christmas lights switch-on. The event, which marks the start of the festive season, is set to draw large crowds to the city centre. Residents planning to travel into the area are advised to prepare for busy conditions throughout the day.

stories.headline: Planning proposals submitted for Ely conservation areas
stories.brief: New planning applications have been submitted that could impact listed buildings and conservation areas in and around Ely. Residents and interested parties are being advised that these proposals are currently under consideration. Details regarding the specific sites and the nature of the planned works are available through the local planning authority. Those living in the area are encouraged to review the documents to understand how these potential changes might affect the local landscape and historic properties.

stories.headline: Earthworks trials planned for proposed Fens Reservoir
stories.brief: Water companies have announced plans to conduct earthworks trials as part of the ongoing development of the proposed Fens Reservoir. The project, which aims to secure future water supplies for the region, will see initial testing carried out to assess the ground conditions. Further details regarding the timeline and specific locations for these trials are expected to be released as the planning process continues. Residents are advised to monitor official updates for any potential impact on local areas.

stories.headline: Springwood High School celebrates best-ever Ofsted report
stories.brief:
Springwood High School in King’s Lynn is celebrating its highest-ever rating following a two-day Ofsted inspection on October 20 and 21. Inspectors praised the school’s positive culture, stable leadership, and excellent pastoral support, describing the environment as feeling like a family. The report highlighted the school’s robust curriculum and a wide range of extra-curricular activities, noting that pupils feel safe and supported.

While the school was commended for its vibrant community spirit, inspectors suggested that leaders should continue to refine strategies for pupils facing multiple barriers to learning. Executive head teacher Andrew Johnson expressed his pride in the staff and students, describing the outcome as a reflection of their daily dedication.

stories.headline: Wisbech veteran honoured with National Service medal
stories.brief:
A 93-year-old Wisbech veteran has been presented with a medal to honour his National Service following the Second World War. Gordon Phoenix, a former member of the medical corps, received the award during a surprise ceremony held at the town’s new veterans hub on Wednesday. 

The medal was funded by local shop workers and community members who organised the presentation to recognise Mr Phoenix’s service. The event was hosted by the Wisbech branch of the Royal British Legion and attended by the veteran’s friends and family. Mr Phoenix is a well-known figure in the local community and an honorary member of the town’s football club.

stories.headline: Medical records accessed unlawfully at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief:
New figures reveal that staff at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn accessed medical records without authorisation on 107 occasions between 2021 and 2026. Hospital management stated that while most incidents involved employees viewing their own files, one case concerned a patient’s records. That specific matter was investigated and reported to the Information Commissioner’s Office. 

The hospital’s director of people and culture, Zoe Baxter, emphasised that staff are regularly reminded that accessing records for personal reasons is unlawful. Across the country, over 3,000 similar incidents were recorded by NHS staff during the same five-year period. The East of England Ambulance Service Trust reported 182 cases of inappropriate access within that timeframe.

stories.headline: Two men charged following jewellery store robbery
stories.brief: Two men have been charged in connection with a raid at a jewellery store. The charges follow an investigation into the incident. No further details regarding the location of the shop or the identities of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: List of Cambridgeshire flats with potentially unsafe cladding published
stories.brief: A list has been released identifying blocks of flats across Cambridgeshire that feature potentially unsafe cladding. The information, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, highlights specific residential buildings within the county that are currently under review regarding their exterior materials. Residents living in high-rise or multi-occupancy accommodation are advised to check the full list to see if their property is included. Further details regarding the safety status of these buildings can be found in the latest report from the Ely Standard.

stories.headline: Traffic disruption following lorry incident in Spalding
stories.brief: Motorists in Spalding are facing delays today after a lorry shed its load at a busy roundabout. Local reports indicate that the incident has caused disruption to traffic flow in the area. Drivers are advised to approach the junction with caution and allow extra time for their journeys while the scene is cleared. No further details regarding the cause of the incident or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Body recovered from river in Cambridgeshire search
stories.brief: Police have recovered a body from a river as part of the search for a missing man from Cambridgeshire. The discovery was reported by the Ely Standard. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the specific location of the recovery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Christmas Golden Age fair returns to Wisbech for over 60s
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council is hosting its Christmas Golden Age fair for residents aged over 60. The free event takes place at the Hudson Leisure Centre in Wisbech on Friday, December 11, between 10am and 1pm. Visitors can enjoy refreshments, entertainment, and access advice on topics including transport, finances, and wellbeing. Attendees will also receive a Christmas gift, provided through a partnership with the How Are You Fenland? project.

The council is still accepting donations of new, unwrapped gifts at local libraries and supermarkets until December 4. The fair is open to older residents, as well as their carers, family members, and advocates. Further details on the event and gift donation points are available via the Fenland District Council website.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn restaurant listed for lease
stories.brief:
The Royal Gourmet Buffet in King’s Lynn has been placed on the market. Located near the Southgates Roundabout, the restaurant has been operating under its current ownership since 2017. The lease is available for £50,000, with the owners citing family commitments for the sale.

The 1,600 square foot premises currently accommodates 60 diners, though agents suggest this capacity could be increased to 100. The site includes a 15-space car park and second-floor living quarters that require refurbishment. Additionally, there is potential to convert the first floor into a House in Multiple Occupation or further residential accommodation.

stories.headline: Earthworks trials planned for proposed Fens Reservoir site
stories.brief: Water companies are set to begin trial earthworks as part of the development process for the proposed Fens Reservoir. The project, which has been reported by the BBC, involves initial ground investigations to assess the site. Residents across the region are advised that these preparatory works are now moving forward. Further updates on the progress of the reservoir plans will be provided as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over King’s Lynn parking proposals
stories.brief:
Residents are voicing strong opposition to proposed changes to car parking at Tuesday Market Place and Common Staithe Quay in King’s Lynn. Critics argue that reducing parking availability will deter visitors from attending events at the Corn Exchange, particularly older and disabled patrons who rely on nearby access. Concerns have been raised that lower attendance could negatively impact the venue’s revenue and the local arts scene.

Meanwhile, other local issues highlighted in recent correspondence include concerns over the presence of dogs in food establishments, the impact of derelict buildings on the town centre, and opposition to the proposed Longmarsh solar array project in West Norfolk.

stories.headline: Ely MP highlights youth unemployment concerns
stories.brief: The Member of Parliament for Ely has issued a formal call for action regarding youth unemployment in the area. The local representative is urging for new measures to be taken to address the issue, as reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. No further details regarding specific proposals or planned initiatives have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Long Sutton waste site operator receives £1 million fine
stories.brief: An operator of an illegal waste site in Long Sutton has been ordered to pay one million pounds in fines. The penalty follows legal action concerning the unauthorised management of waste at the location. No further details regarding the operator or the specific nature of the site have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police apply to close ten shops over illegal goods
stories.brief: Police are seeking closure orders for ten shops following the discovery of illegal goods. The applications were reported by the BBC, though specific locations for the businesses have not been disclosed. Authorities are pursuing these legal measures as part of an ongoing effort to address the sale of illicit items. Further details regarding which premises are affected or when the court hearings will take place remain unavailable at this time.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council approves land sale for new ambulance hub
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council has agreed to sell three and a half acres of land at Morston Drift in South Lynn to the East of England Ambulance Service. The site is set to be transformed into a new ambulance base serving the local area and beyond. 

The land, which was previously considered for housing and business use, has been identified by the NHS Trust as an ideal location for its operations. The council plans to proceed with the sale once the ambulance service secures the necessary planning permission. While the authority confirmed it will receive a capital receipt from the transaction, the specific financial details have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Body recovered from river in Cambridgeshire search
stories.brief: Police have recovered a body from a river during the search for a missing man from Cambridgeshire. The discovery was reported by the Cambs Times. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the specific location of the recovery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Terrington St Clement man cleared of assault charges
stories.brief:
A 22-year-old man from Terrington St Clement has been cleared of assault and stalking charges at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Ryley Dale, of Waterloo Road, had faced allegations including intentional strangulation, criminal damage, and harassment of an ex-partner between 2023 and 2024. During a summary trial on Wednesday, November 11, the Crown Prosecution Service offered no evidence, leading to the charges being dropped.

Mr. Dale previously gained public attention in September 2024 for his actions during a house fire in Gaywood. He was credited with helping to save four people from the property on Lynn Road after forcing entry to the building.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Under-21s draw with Bolton Wanderers
stories.brief: The Peterborough United Under-21 side has finished their latest fixture with a share of the points. The match against Bolton Wanderers ended in a one-all draw.
